name: Student residence permit

requirements.blocker_text: Requires admission to a full-time programme (bachelor's, master's, PhD, or equivalent) at a Danish state-approved educational institution -- students admitted to institutions that are not state-approved face restricted employment rights, no post-study job-search permit, and limits on family reunification.
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission to a Danish state-approved institution rather than a non-approved one to access the full set of associated rights.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires documented proof of sufficient funds to cover living costs for the duration of study.
requirements.fix_path: Provide bank statements, a scholarship award letter, or a sponsor's financial guarantee.

evidence_required.document: Admission letter from a Danish state-approved institution
Proof of funds for living costs
Health insurance (until CPR registration, after which public healthcare applies)

sources.title: Nyidanmark.dk -- official Danish immigration portal, Study category, distinguishing state-approved from non-approved institutions

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING, a real and consequential two-tier system confirmed via a January 2026 tightening: Denmark distinguishes sharply between students at state-approved institutions (full part-time work rights, eligibility for a post-study job-search residence permit, and normal family-reunification access) and students at institutions that are not state-approved, who face restricted employment rights, no post-study job-search permit, and limits on family reunification -- these restrictions were confirmed as continuing into 2026 rather than being phased out. Students on this permit may generally work part-time (commonly cited as up to 20 hours/week during term and full-time during official holiday periods, though the exact current cap was not independently confirmed against a primary nyidanmark.dk page in this research pass) -- work_rights is modeled 'restricted' to reflect this real but capped allowance. switchable_to points to the employer-sponsored work route as the standard graduate pathway; Denmark's post-study job-search permit (Etableringskort/jobsøgningsopholdstilladelse) functions as an intermediate bridging status for state-approved-institution graduates specifically, not modeled as its own separate route file here given its narrow, transitional nature, but flagged as a candidate for future expansion.
